newsitem.title: UK: UK nuclear reprocessing plant shutdown.
newsitem.headline: UK nuclear reprocessing plant shutdown.

text.p: A nuclear reprocessing plant at the state-run Dounreay complex in Scotland has been shut down after slightly higher than normal levels of radiation were found in a waste tank, a spokesman said on Monday.
The spokesman said a very small amount of radiation had entered a cooling system but there was no danger to staff or the public.
"Monitoring equipment detected a very small amount of radioactivity in a tank of waste being discharged into the sea," the spokesman told Reuters.
"At no time were members of the workforce or the public at any risk," he added.
He said it was not clear how long the reprocessing plant involved -- one of two at Dounreay -- would remain shut.
"Engineers are working on the problem at the moment. It could be very short or it could be several months. Reprocessing of PFR fuel will stop for the moment," the spokesman said.
The spokesman said the amount of radioactivity found was seven gigabequerels. The site's annual authorised discharge level is 750 gigabequerels.
